 October 5, 2026 • 488 words 

The Northeast’s leading supply chain provider will now offer warehousing and LTL transportation services out of its Camp Hill site, giving customers faster, more flexible distribution across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Ohio

WEST CHESTER, Pa. — October 5, 2026 — A. Duie Pyle (Pyle), a premier, 102-year-old family-owned and operated provider of asset and non-asset-based supply chain solutions, today announces the opening of a new warehouse facility in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania. Positioned directly adjacent to the company’s existing less-than-truckload (LTL) service center, the facility transforms the site into a fully integrated logistics center that brings warehousing and transportation operations together on one connected campus, providing customers with greater speed, flexibility and supply chain efficiency.

## LTL carrier’s North American terminal count reaches 300 

 Todd Maiden 

· Thursday, October 01, 2026 

 XPO expanded its North American footprint to 300 terminals following the addition of new service centers in Missouri and Arizona. (Photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves) 

Less-than-truckload carrier XPO announced Thursday that it has added new locations in Arizona and Missouri, increasing its terminal count to 300 across North America.

A new 51,000-square-foot facility in Mesa, Arizona has 86 dock doors and over 100 employees. The terminal gives XPO (NYSE: XPO) needed capacity to serve the Phoenix market, where it already operates a freight assembly center. The region is experiencing an increase in demand given recent industrial investments and growing cross-border trade with Mexico.

A 13,000-square-foot terminal in Cameron, Missouri (approximately 50 miles north of Kansas City) has 32 dock doors and over 30 employees. It sits near the intersection of I-35 and U.S. 36, serving both north-south and east-west freight corridors.

# Next era of intermodal growth at Rickenbacker

 Oct 01, 2026 

 

The first site-specific story in a series highlighting the investments shaping Norfolk Southern's intermodal network.

Key points

- Rickenbacker Intermodal Facility in Columbus, Ohio, is nearing completion of a major expansion to increase capacity, improve ramp operations and add flexibility across international lanes.
- Norfolk Southern has invested more than $30 million since the terminal opened in 2008.
- Pad track capacity is up 70% versus the original footprint; modeled capacity is growing from about 250,000 lifts per year in 2008 to roughly 410,000 once Phases 3 and 4 are complete.
- The facility handled 335,607 verified lifts in 2025.
- Rickenbacker gives Columbus-market customers the flexibility to route to either coast within a day’s drive of a large share of the U.S. population — inland-gateway optionality that lets them adjust as supply chains shift.

#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

# Gofo parcel network quickly mushrooms in 2026

## New Dallas hub offers more room, automation to handle volume growth as peak season approaches 

 Eric Kulisch 

· Thursday, August 27, 2026 

 Gofo’s new Dallas warehouse is twice the size of the previous facility, allowing it to process more parcels while improving efficiency. (Photo: Gofo) 

Parcel delivery startup Gofo has doubled the capacity of its Dallas processing center after moving into a new building and installing automated sortation equipment, as it races other regional carriers to build national scale.

The larger terminal comes on line ahead of the peak season rush, allowing the company to absorb greater volume in the central United States rather than adding temporary facilities mid-season. Gofo says it expects parcel volume to jump 50% above normal weekly levels during the period between Thanksgiving and Christmas.
